{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) result in statistically significant differences in mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a One-Way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "Null Hypothesis (H0): The mean performance is equal across all five stimulation paradigms (e.g., mean Time-to-Target_combined = mean Time-to-Target_sham).",
    "Alternative Hypothesis (H1): At least one stimulation paradigm mean differs from the others.",
    "Significance threshold: alpha = 0.05.",
    "For each variable: If F-statistic p-value < 0.05, reject H0 and proceed to post-hoc analysis.",
    "If ANOVA assumptions are violated for Time-to-Target (due to potential kurtosis from max=201.39) and Average Speed, apply a log transformation or use a non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis) before final inference."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of Observations: Assumed based on experimental design; verify no repeated measures within the same row entry.",
    "Normality of Residuals: Inspect Q-Q plots of residuals for each ANOVA model. Note: Time-to-Target has a large range (0.5 to 201.39) which may cause non-normality; check skewness/kurtosis.",
    "Homogeneity of Variances (Homoscedasticity): Levene's Test or Bartlett's Test must be applied to residuals across the 5 groups. Critical for ANOVA validity.",
    " influential Outliers: Identify and inspect rows with extreme values (e.g., Time-to-Target > 100) to ensure they do not drive Group Means disproportionately.",
    "Scale Check: Verify that 'Success' (0-1) and 'Path Efficiency' (0-29) distributions meet ANOVA requirements or require transformation."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If global F-test is significant (p < 0.05), conduct pairwise comparisons between all 5 levels of 'Stim Paradigm'.",
    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) method for multiple comparisons to control the Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER).",
    "Report Contrast Estimates with 95% Confidence Intervals for each significant pairwise difference.",
    "If homogeneity of variance fails (Levene's p < 0.05), switch to Games-Howell post-hoc test which does not assume equal variances.",
    "For non-parametric results (if Kruskal-Wallis is used), report Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' stimulus likely yields the shortest Time-to-Target and highest Average Speed compared to 'Sham' (high.weapon_count in Combined suggests high stimulation intensity).",
    "Success rates may be highest in visual-only or combined conditions versus Sham, assuming navigation is visual-motor dependent.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) is expected to be lowest in 'Combined' or visual conditions (sharp turning) and highest in 'Sham' (erratic movement).",
    "Path Efficiency may differ significantly, with stimulated groups showing more direct paths than the Sham group.",
    "Dim Visual Only may perform similarly to Bright Visual Only or both may outperform Sham if vision drives navigation, despite the 'Dim' qualifier potentially reducing performance relative to Bright."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Skewness in 'Time-to-Target' (max ~201 vs mean ~2.8) may breach normality assumptions for standard ANOVA, necessitating robust methods or transformation.",
    "Unequal group sample sizes (n_Combined=48846 vs n_Sham=3505) increases Type II error risk for smaller groups and complicates variance estimation; Welch's ANOVA is a recommended alternative if variances are unequal.",
    "'Path Efficiency' has a very wide range (0.0009 to 29.8); if this represents distance or time ratios, the distribution may be highly non-normal.",
    "Analysis is purely observational based on the provided summary; biological confounds (e.g., individual mouse differences across the 8 Mouse levels) are aggregated in the 'Stim Paradigm' factor and cannot be controlled for in this specific ANOVA model without the raw data.",
    "Categorical variable 'Success' (0/1) is technically binomial; while mean comparison works, Proportions Z-test might be more theoretically sound than ANOVA if the distribution is heavily skewed toward 0 or 1, though valid if n per group is large."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct Welch's One-Way ANOVA (to handle potential unequal variances) and Levene's Test for homogeneity of variance on the raw data, followed by Logistic Regression for 'Success' and Generalized Linear Models (GLM) with Gamma distribution for 'Path Efficiency' and skewed continuous variables if assumptions fail."
}
